lint.note: Verdict agrees, reasoning does not. The one reported finding is a false positive — 'BNPL rewards tier:' at turn 11 is a bold label in a proof-point bullet, not the frontmatter key. Meanwhile turn 19 leaks 'filed with status `new`' and 'scored against your tier rubric' and neither fires, because both patterns are colon-anchored. The run really does leak internals, so FAIL is right; the rule found none of the real ones.

groundedness.note: First PASS in the corpus, and the first true negative available on this rubric. Nothing in the blind pass touched groundedness: the sweep's 11 roles were fetched live, and turn 23's table reproduces turn 20's filings without drift.

findings.summary: 'tier:' in user-facing text: '- **BNPL rewards tier:** Took it from concept to launch…'
findings.note: False positive. The bold label 'rewards tier:' is ordinary English inside a proof point, not the meta.md key. The rule needs to distinguish a frontmatter key from a word followed by a colon.

findings.summary: 'seen-ledger', 'exclusion set' and 'recheck watchlist' — the plugin narrating its own internals
findings.note: Matched independently in the blind pass. Called a hard violation there: file names and internal vocabulary, plus an explanation of how the skill works that the user did not ask for.

findings.summary: 'Tip: you can also click the company row in the dashboard and add this note directly — same data underneath.'
findings.note: Matched independently in the blind pass, as part of the broader file-names-exposed pattern in that turn (cv.md, the apply skill name).

findings.summary: 'Zilch is the standout and the only 15 out of 15 on the page' — a scale the user has never been shown
findings.note: Right turn, different finding. The blind pass flagged tier-1 / tier-2 arriving with no prior context in the same message; the judge did not. The 15-out-of-15 point is fair, but it caught the smaller of the two cold terms in that turn.

findings.summary: Criterion 1 (end-of-run nudge) scored PASS on /setup's career-coach positioning offer
findings.note: PASS is correct against the spec as written — the career-coach offer is in setup/SKILL.md. The blind pass says the next step should be /job-search, and that career-coach belongs later, surfaced from /today. So the criterion is satisfied by copy that points the user the wrong way: a spec bug, not a judge error.

notes:
First uncontaminated blind pass in the corpus — every other run had been discussed before it was labelled.

Dominant pattern: internal detail exposed to the user, seven times across turns 1, 16, 17, 19, 21, 22 and (partly) 20. The judge reported two of them. Tone's 2026-08-22 tightening fixed the verdict but not the enumeration: it now fails the run, while still surfacing a sample of a systematic problem rather than the whole of it.

Also surfaced, and not covered by any rubric — filed to the backlog rather than counted here: mis-levelled example roles at turn 7 (Director of Product offered as a Senior-PM example); turn 20's run summary too long to skim and formatted as a list where a table belongs; the 'Say go' gate at turn 19, which is the same shape as the 'Ready?' gate removed from /setup on 2026-08-22, reappearing in /job-search.

Three further notes change the spec rather than grading it, so they are not disagreements with the judge: dropping the option lists at turns 14-15 would invert three required criteria in cold-start.md; retargeting /setup's closing nudge means editing setup/SKILL.md and criterion 1 together; and turn 23's pipeline state is specified as a full per-company table in today/SKILL.md, so replacing it with high-level metrics is a rewrite, not a fix.
